claims.text: The baseline is a conventional aluminum–lithium alloy containing less than 4 wt% lithium.
Standard heat treatment of the baseline alloy results in a coarser microstructure.
Increasing the lithium content to approximately 4 wt% will reduce alloy density relative to a lower-lithium baseline.
Solution treatment at approximately 500°C for 2 hours followed by aging at approximately 150°C for 10 hours will improve the alloy's comprehensive mechanical performance.
The proposed composition and heat treatment will increase strength relative to conventional lower-lithium aluminum–lithium alloys.
The proposed composition and heat treatment will increase toughness relative to conventional lower-lithium aluminum–lithium alloys.
The proposed composition and heat treatment will improve corrosion resistance relative to conventional lower-lithium aluminum–lithium alloys.
The proposed processing will produce a refined microstructure containing finer precipitates.
The proposed processing will improve the distribution of strengthening phases.
Higher lithium content and the controlled heat treatment promote nucleation of fine precipitates.
Fine precipitates reinforce the alloy structure and thereby enhance strength.
The proposed precipitate-mediated structural changes enhance corrosion resistance.
The predicted improvements depend on maintaining the specified composition and heat-treatment conditions.
Performance under environmental or loading conditions different from those specified remains unverified.
The magnitude of the strength increase and density reduction may depend on processing precision and alloy purity.
